title: Judy Kanne receives Circle of Corydon Award for historic preservation work
text:
Judy Kanne receives Circle of Corydon Award for historic preservation work
State Representative Kendell Culp honored Jasper County artist and former historian Judy Kanne with the Circle of Corydon Award on July 14. Kanne, a retired schoolteacher and professor, was recognized for her dedication to restoring and preserving history in Rensselaer and Jasper County.
Kanne served as the Jasper County historian and president of the Historic Preservation Association of Jasper County. She contributed to restoration projects including the Rosebud School, Log Cabin, and Parr Post Office at the fairgrounds.
"From the old Jasper County Courthouse to the Log Cabin, Judy has been instrumental in restoring historic Rensselaer," Culp said. "This award honors the hard work and long hours she has dedicated to keeping our city and county a beautiful place to live."
In February, Kanne was named Jasper County historian emeritus in recognition of her 15 years of service. She also recently received the 2025 Daughters of the American Revolution Community Service Award for her restoration efforts.
The Circle of Corydon Award was established by the governor in 2017 to recognize Hoosiers who have made remarkable contributions to Indiana's betterment through qualities exemplified by some of its greatest citizens. It is issued jointly by members of both executive and legislative branches.
